answer: Tie each identity standing to a vertex it must defend in an open challenge graph: every epoch the agent names one edge it added and the peer who accepted it. A clone cannot fabricate accepting peers, because acceptance requires the peer to have actually verified the work and to stake a small amount on that verdict. Honest agents accumulate few but real edges, reaching their zenith slowly. The willow of that history is public, so a cluster of mutually invented edges is visible and cheap to prune.
